'''Albrecht Fröhlich''' {{post-nominals|country=GBR|FRS}}<ref name="frs"/> (22 May 1916 – 8 November 2001) was a German-born British mathematician, famous for his major results and [[conjectures]] on [[Galois module]] theory in the Galois structure of rings of integers.<ref name="frs">{{Cite journal | last1 = Birch | first1 = B. J. | last2 = Taylor | first2 = M. J. | doi = 10.1098/rsbm.2005.0010 | title = Albrecht Frahlich 22 May 1916 - 8 November 2001: Elected FRS 1976 | journal = [[Biographical Memoirs of Fellows of the Royal Society]] | volume = 51 | pages = 149 | year = 2005 | doi-access = free }}</ref>

==Education==
He was born in [[Munich]] to a [[Jew]]ish family.  He fled from the [[Nazism|Nazi]]s to [[France]], and then to [[Mandatory Palestine|Palestine]].  He went to [[Bristol University]] in 1945, gaining a B.Sc. in 1948 and a Ph.D. in 1951 with a dissertation entitled ''On Some Topics in the Theory of Representation of Groups and Individual Class Field Theory '' under the supervision of [[Hans Heilbronn]].  He was a lecturer at the [[University of Leicester]] and then at the [[University of Keele|Keele University]], then in 1962 moved as reader to [[King's College London]] where he worked until his retirement in 1981 when he moved to [[Robinson College, Cambridge]].

==Awards==
He was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] in 1976.<ref name="frs"/> He was awarded the [[Berwick Prizes|Berwick Prize]] of the [[London Mathematical Society]] in 1976 and its [[De Morgan Medal]] in 1992. The Society's [[Fröhlich Prize]] is named in his honour.

==Personal==
He is the brother of [[Herbert Fröhlich]].
